bibliography.title: Novel Design and Optimization of Porous Titanium Structure for Mandibular Reconstruction
bibliography.authors: Liu R, Su Y, Yang W, Dang X, Zhang C, Du R, Zhong Y.

study.research_problem: A mandibular scaffold should be anatomically conforming, highly interconnected and porous, yet remain below a mechanical stress limit; uniform periodic trimming can create free ends and waste material in low-stress regions.
study.exact_gap: Prior approaches did not simultaneously avoid surface free ends/steps, control peak stress to a chosen target, improve stress utilization, and maximize porosity in a mandibular defect-specific scaffold (S002:C02-S002:C05).
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Generate a contour-conforming tetrahedral network from one reconstructed mandible, iteratively assign 0.3-0.6 mm strut diameters using two clenching-load FE results, and demonstrate a higher-porosity design whose predicted peak stress remains below a target (S001:C01; S003:C01-S006:C03).
study.study_design: A single CT-derived mandibular defect and two fixation plates/six screws were modeled; an initial 0.4 mm, 2.4 mm-cell tetrahedral structure was iteratively resized for 120, 100, or 80 MPa targets, analyzed under incisal and unilateral molar clenching, and selected designs were printed in Ti6Al4V (S003:C01-S011:C01).
study.sample_or_model: One patient CT geometry simplified to cortical bone, idealized plates/screws and a fully bonded late-healing scaffold; linear isotropic homogeneous material models and literature muscle forces were used (S003:C01-S005:C02; S012:C03-S012:C07).
comparators: Optimized structures constrained at 120, 100, and 80 MPa (models B-D)
Incisal clenching versus left unilateral molar clenching
No solid implant, conventional lattice, topology-optimized alternative, experimental mandible, or animal comparator
method_spine: Reconstruct and simplify one mandible and define defect/fixation geometry.
Tetrahedralize the design volume and replace mesh edges with cylindrical struts.
Assign simplified materials, fully integrated contacts, constraints, and two static muscle-load cases.
Iteratively resize each strut on a 0.05 mm grid within manufacturing bounds until both load cases meet a peak-stress target while reducing weight.
Compare designed porosity, peak stress, strut-size distribution, and stress histogram.
Print the design and treat manufacturability, as-built fidelity, mechanics, fatigue, permeability, and biology as separate validation stages.

verification: Mesh sensitivity is stated to converge at 123,268 elements, but alternative meshes, convergence plots, and tolerances are not reported (S005:C01; S012:C03).
Optimization convergence is shown over eight iterations for the 120 MPa target, and peak stress is checked in both prescribed load cases (S006:C01-S006:C03; S010:C01).
calibration: The 120 MPa target is derived by multiplying an approximate mandibular peak stress (17 MPa) by the Ti-to-bone modulus ratio to seek a similar strain stimulus; it is a mechanobiological design heuristic, not patient-specific calibration (S006:C03).
Strut bounds and 0.05 mm increments are chosen from assumed SLM capability, without measured machine/material calibration (S004:C01).
validation: Printing intact struts and measuring mass demonstrate basic manufacturability, not as-built geometric or mechanical validation (S011:C01).

No coupon/scaffold compression, tension, bending, fatigue, permeability, CT metrology, cadaveric mandible, animal defect, or clinical validation is performed; the conclusion requests mechanical and animal tests (S013:C01).
sensitivity: Three target stresses and two clenching loads expose the porosity-stress tradeoff (S006:C03-S009:C03).

No uncertainty analysis varies muscle forces, missing teeth/contact, healing stage, bone properties, contact/bonding, extreme loads, fatigue spectrum, AM defects, or patient geometry (S012:C03-S012:C07).
application_prediction: Stress, strain, porosity, material utilization, stress shielding, fatigue safety, permeability, and bone-growth stimulation are model/application claims under ideal assumptions; only geometry and mass were physically demonstrated.

primary_outcomes: The initial model had designed porosity 66.83% and predicted peaks of 91.69 MPa (incisal) and 129.78 MPa (unilateral molar) (S009:C01-S009:C02).

The 120 MPa design reached 80.31% designed porosity and predicted peaks 87.57/118.12 MPa; the 100 and 80 MPa designs reached 79.15% and 73.23% porosity with correspondingly lower peaks (S008:C01-S009:C02).

For the selected 120 MPa design, 92.1% of struts were at the minimum 0.3 mm size and at least 64.1% remained below 20 MPa, so stress use was more even than the baseline but still far from homogeneous (S008:C01-S009:C03; S012:C04-S012:C05).
Mandible/fixation-system high-stress locations and peaks changed little after scaffold optimization, with screw 3 and condylar regions remaining critical (S007:C01).
SLM produced visually intact connected structures, and measured mass fell from 11.48 to 8.17 g; no nominal-to-as-built strut or pore measurement was reported (S011:C01).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Numerically verified single-geometry sizing optimization plus qualitative printability/mass demonstration; no calibrated as-built mechanics, fatigue, transport, biological, animal, or clinical evidence.

argument_map.central_claim: Discrete stress-guided strut resizing can reduce modeled mass and raise designed porosity while satisfying chosen peak-stress targets under two idealized loads, but the selected design's fatigue safety, permeability, mechanobiological stimulus, and reconstructive efficacy remain unvalidated.
data: One CT-derived FE model, two static muscle-load cases, three stress targets, iteration histories, porosity/stress/diameter distributions, and printed masses (S003:C01-S011:C01).
The paper's own limitations identify ideal muscle loads, limited load cases, fully healed bonding, and need for mechanical/animal tests (S012:C03-S013:C01).
argument_map.warrant: Within a fixed model and manufacturing design space, meeting explicit stress constraints while reducing material is a valid engineering improvement; translation requires confirming every assumption that couples design to as-built structure, cyclic mechanics, transport, and bone response.
backing: The target sweep demonstrates an expected porosity-versus-stress tradeoff and the printed design establishes at least basic realizability (S008:C01-S011:C01).
argument_map.qualifier: Algorithmic feasibility for one geometry and two static idealized loads.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: The target stress is a heuristic based on modulus ratio and approximate peak stress, not a validated mechanoregulation window (S006:C03).
Linear elastic solid Ti properties ignore AM surface roughness, porosity, anisotropy, defects, residual stress, and size effects.
Fully bonded late-healing contact excludes early fixation micromotion and evolving osseointegration (S012:C07).
Two static clenching cases do not represent extreme, oblique, impact, or cyclic mastication loads (S012:C06-S012:C07).
Static peak von Mises stress cannot be compared directly with a nominal 900 MPa fatigue limit to guarantee safe use (S009:C01; S012:C05-S012:C07).
Designed porosity does not establish as-built porosity, permeability, cell ingress, vascularization, or bone growth.
The heuristic stops at a feasible discrete solution and the authors acknowledge it is not a global optimum (S012:C05).

measured: One source CT geometry and printed masses/visual connectivity (S003:C01; S011:C01).
predicted: All mandible, screw, plate, and scaffold stress/strain distributions; designed porosity; target satisfaction; and material-utilization metrics are FE/CAD outputs (S005:C01-S010:C01).
inferred: Similar scaffold and bone strain is inferred to reduce stress shielding and stimulate ingrowth via a mechanostat argument (S006:C03; S009:C01; S012:C05).
Higher designed porosity is inferred to improve permeability, cell/nutrient exchange, and lightweight reconstruction (S001:C01; S012:C01-S012:C02; S013:C01).
Peak static stress far below a literature fatigue limit is inferred to ensure fatigue safety (S009:C01; S012:C05-S012:C07).
recommended: Add CT metrology and surface/defect characterization, as-built coupon/scaffold cyclic tests, model updating, early-to-late healing contacts, multi-activity probabilistic loads, permeability/transport, animal segmental defect, and multi-patient validation.
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: FE target satisfaction is not physical strength or fatigue validation.
Static peak stress below a coupon fatigue limit is not a device fatigue-life prediction.
Designed porosity is not measured permeability or tissue ingrowth.
Predicted strain similarity is not observed mechanobiological stimulation.
A visually intact print is not nominal-to-as-built fidelity or quality assurance.
overclaim_risks: The claim that the target is far below fatigue failure and therefore 'ensures safe use' ignores AM fatigue and loading uncertainties (S012:C07).
The conclusion calls the design a good reconstructive choice before mechanical or animal experiments (S013:C01).
The discussion says porosity was 'improved by 80.31%' although 80.31% is the final porosity; the reported increase is 13.48 percentage points (S010:C01; S012:C04).
The automatic animal cue is false; no animal experiment was performed.

section_moves.move: State an explicit objective, constraint, variable set, and manufacturable discretization
section_moves.execution: The paper defines weight minimization, peak-stress constraint across two loads, per-strut diameter variables, and 0.3-0.6 mm discrete bounds (S006:C01-S006:C03).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Topology/sizing papers should declare objective, every load-case constraint, design variables, manufacturing bounds, stopping rule, and whether the solution is local/heuristic or global.
section_moves.failure_mode: A precisely stated optimization can still optimize the wrong or unvalidated target.

section_moves.move: Show the Pareto-like target tradeoff rather than one selected design
section_moves.execution: Models B-D reveal that lower target stress requires thicker struts and reduces porosity, while all improve over the uniform baseline (S008:C01-S009:C03).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Report the constraint sweep with objective value, stress, porosity/mass, diameter distribution, and rationale for selecting one operating point.
section_moves.failure_mode: Calling one target optimal requires a validated decision criterion, not only closeness to a heuristic strain.

section_moves.move: Separate CAD feasibility from as-built validation
section_moves.execution: The printed structure is visually intact and weighed, but no CT or mechanical comparison to CAD/FE is provided (S011:C01).
section_moves.transferable_principle: After optimization, report CAD geometry, manufactured geometry, defect/surface state, and tested mechanics as distinct states and quantify loss at every transition.
section_moves.failure_mode: 'Printable' does not mean geometrically faithful or mechanically validated.

section_moves.move: Propagate load/healing assumptions into claim scope
section_moves.execution: The authors identify idealized muscle forces, two load cases, omitted extremes, and assumed late-stage bonding (S012:C03; S012:C06-S012:C07).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For each optimization assumption, state which constraints may be violated outside it and prohibit safety/biology claims until those scenarios are tested.
section_moves.failure_mode: Listing limitations while still claiming guaranteed fatigue safety is internally inconsistent.

author_reported: Ideal dentition/mandibular loading, assumed unchanged healthy muscle forces, only two common clenching states, possible extreme-load exceedance, assumed late-stage union, limited diameter range, and non-global optimization (S012:C03-S012:C07).
Mechanical tests and animal segmental-defect experiments are still required (S013:C01).
reader_identified: One patient geometry and no patient/load/material uncertainty.
Mesh convergence and numerical verification are asserted without quantitative evidence.
No calibration of AM strut dimensions, material anisotropy, defects, roughness, residual stress, or fatigue properties.
No nominal-to-as-built CT metrology; only visual completeness and mass.
No scaffold-level mechanical, fatigue, permeability, or transport experiment.
Peak-stress target and mechanostat interpretation are heuristic and not validated against bone response.
No early fixation/micromotion, remodeling, animal, or clinical evidence.
The final-porosity versus improvement wording is numerically inconsistent.
likely_bias_direction: Ideal bonding and static loads likely understate critical stresses/micromotion during healing.
Nominal solid-material properties and absence of AM defects likely overstate fatigue margin.
Designed porosity and mechanostat reasoning likely overstate permeability and osteogenic benefit.
limitations.scope_boundary: The study demonstrates a discrete FE strut-sizing method and basic printability for one late-healed mandibular model; it does not validate as-built mechanics, fatigue safety, permeability, bone ingrowth, or reconstructive effectiveness.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Write lattice sizing/topology optimization with explicit objective, load-case constraints, variables, manufacturing bounds, target sweep, stopping rule, and solution-status qualifier.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Optimization Methods, Results tradeoff table, and reproducibility audit.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Meeting a heuristic stress target under two loads is not proof of global optimality or clinical safety.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Track optimized geometry through CAD, as-built metrology, material/defect state, mechanical test, and model-updating gates before biological application claims.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: AM Results, validation plan, and Discussion boundaries.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: An intact print and mass reduction do not establish strut fidelity, fatigue, permeability, or tissue ingrowth.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Audit fatigue and mechanobiology claims for scale, loading, material state, healing contact, and proxy-to-outcome gaps.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Static von Mises stress below a coupon fatigue limit and strain near bone do not guarantee device fatigue or osteogenesis.

critical_weaknesses: One idealized late-healed model and heuristic target.
No as-built metrology or mechanical/fatigue validation.
Porosity, fatigue, and osteogenic claims exceed measured evidence.

summary_zh: 该研究用一个患者的下颌 CT 构建缺损与固定系统，把四面体网格边替换为支杆，并在 0.3–0.6 mm、0.05 mm 步长内按两种静态咬合载荷调整每根支杆。120 MPa 方案的设计孔隙率从 66.83% 提到 80.31%，峰值落在目标下；但 120 MPa 来自‘骨峰值应力×钛/骨模量比’的启发式推导，不是经实验校准的机械生物学阈值。打印件只做了视觉完整性和质量测量，没有 CT 的 nominal-to-as-built 计量、材料缺陷、力学/疲劳或渗透测试。模型还假设晚期完全结合，使用理想肌力和两种静态载荷。Skill 将把优化目标/约束/变量/制造界限/目标扫描写清，并强制设置 CAD→as-built→机械试验→模型更新→动物验证五道门；静态峰值远低于名义疲劳极限不等于疲劳安全，设计孔隙率也不等于渗透或骨长入。
reader_notes: Primary Codex reader reviewed every non-reference packet section, including equations, pseudocode description, target rationale, all model comparisons, manufacturing note, and seven-part Discussion.
The automatic animal cue is incorrect; no biological or animal experiment was performed.
The paper is a useful explicit-constraint optimization example and a strong counterexample for FE-to-fatigue/biology overreach.
